candidate.title: Pu-seq
candidate.scope: The Pu-seq (polymerase usage sequencing) row of the assigned Illumina poster: ribonucleotide-containing genomic DNA through alkali treatment, random-primer/Klenow copying with dUTP, adapter attachment, USER treatment and PCR/purification to DNA library. The adjacent 5-C, PB-seq and Break-seq rows are separate context, with no connecting arrows to Pu-seq; the Origin of replication icon describes its biological purpose, not a separate capture operation. The matched primary implementation uses separately prepared S. pombe Polε- and Polδ-mutant libraries in an RNase H2-deficient background. The single drawn path is a library-preparation architecture, not a complete protocol or a claim that every Pu-seq implementation uses identical preparation. Sequencing and comparison of mutant-source datasets explain what the resulting library represents but are not added as unshown operations.

states.label: Ribonucleotide-containing genomic duplex DNA
features: The drawing labels antiparallel 5′/3′ ends and an embedded R; the adjacent Origin of replication icon describes the biological target, not a captured origin substrate or separate operation.

Primary-paper context: separate S. pombe RNase H2-deficient (rnh201Δ) strains carry ribonucleotide-discriminating Polε cdc20–M630F or Polδ cdc6–L591G alleles. The schematic is one library-preparation path applied separately; it does not depict mixing these samples.
Embedded ribonucleotides mark synthesis by the respective mutant polymerase; the material sequenced is DNA, not polymerase protein or cellular RNA.

evidence.rationale: dUTP was introduced during complementary-strand synthesis; the specifically named USER step then interrupts that strand in the drawing. Together with the paper’s strand-directed library design, this supports selective disruption of the copy and retention of original-strand orientation, without asserting perfect removal.

states.label: PCR-amplified and purified DNA sequencing library
features: Terminal poster product is labelled DNA and drawn as one blue line; it follows the indexed, USER-treated material through PCR and purification.

The physical readout carrier is adapter-bearing DNA. In the primary implementation, the R1 5′ position reports the original alkali-generated ssDNA 5′ boundary, assigning a ribonucleotide position and genomic strand.

Polymerase usage is inferred from the separately identified mutant-source libraries and strand-resolved counts, rather than from a polymerase-specific sequence tag. These data support replication-origin location and efficiency; replication timing is indirect.

operations.label: Alkali treatment
operations.description: Cleaves genomic DNA at embedded ribonucleotides and denatures it into ssDNA fragments. This changes an internal ribonucleotide mark into a fragment boundary, rather than converting R to U. The explicit ssDNA boundary is resolved from the primary paper because the poster compresses the cleavage/copying stages.
operations.mechanism: Alkali-dependent phosphate-backbone cleavage 3′ to ribose generates a 5′-OH on one product and a cyclic 2′,3′ phosphate on the other.
operations.information_effect: The newly generated 5′ boundary retains positional information about an incorporated ribonucleotide. Interpreting those boundaries as polymerase usage also requires the original sample’s polymerase-mutant identity and strand-resolved readout.

operations.label: Klenow reaction(+ random primer, dATP, dGTP,dCTP, dUTP)
operations.description: Uses the alkali-derived ssDNA as a template for random-primer extension to make duplex DNA. dUTP in the copying reaction marks the newly synthesized complementary strand with U; extension reaches a flush end adjacent to the ribonucleotide-defined boundary.
operations.mechanism: Random-primer DNA synthesis with the depicted Klenow reaction and dATP, dGTP, dCTP and dUTP; the paper specifies random hexamer priming and replacement of dTTP by dUTP.
operations.information_effect: Retains the original genomic template and its 5′ boundary while making its complementary copy selectively identifiable by incorporated dU.

corrections.diagram_observation: The poster uses a compact duplex-like glyph marked U after the Alkali treatment arrow, beside the Klenow reaction caption, then shows another U-marked duplex before adapter attachment. It does not explicitly separate an alkali-cleaved ssDNA intermediate. The literal U-marked drawings and their order are retained as diagram evidence; they do not by themselves establish conversion of R into U.
corrections.primary_statement: The full text explicitly states that alkali cleaves 3′ to ribose to generate a 5′-OH and that denatured DNA templates random-primer extension. Its library-production methods convert purified ssDNA to dsDNA with dUTP replacing dTTP. Accordingly s_alkali is explicitly authored as the primary-paper-resolved ssDNA intermediate, and s_copy as the dU-containing complementary-strand product.
